profile.summary: CARP is a family of protein language models built from convolutions rather than attention. Each model reads an amino acid sequence and was pretrained to fill in masked residues, on the March 2020 release of UniRef50. It returns a representation for every residue, plus per-residue logits that can be used to score sequences. Because it is a convolutional network, cost grows linearly with length rather than quadratically.
profile.summary_source_locator: README: Convolutional autoencoding representations of proteins (CARP); abstract

summary_quotes.text: We make available pretrained CNN protein sequence masked language models of various sizes. All of these have a ByteNet encoder architecture and are pretrained on the March 2020 release of UniRef50 using the same masked language modeling task as in BERT and ESM-1b.
convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, which scale linearly with sequence length, could be as effective as transformers in protein language models

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Each CARP model is a ByteNet encoder: stacked convolutional layers with growing dilation, so a residue's representation takes in a widening window of neighbours without attention. Pretraining masks residues and asks the model to predict them, as in BERT and ESM-1b. The loader reads the width, depth, kernel size and dilation factor from the checkpoint and builds a ByteNetLM over the protein alphabet, then wraps it so padding is masked. Forward returns per-residue representations; with repr_layers and logits you also get intermediate layers and the vocabulary logits.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Four sizes are released and are chosen by name in load_model_and_alphabet: carp_600k, carp_38M, carp_76M and carp_640M. The loader fetches each from one Zenodo deposit, so a result should name the checkpoint and that deposit (record 6564798, dated 2022-03-18). The same loader also serves MIF, MIF-ST and BiGCARP from other deposits; MIF-ST pulls carp_640M in as its sequence model, so a MIF-ST result is not a CARP result.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: ByteNet encoder: stacked dilated convolutional layers. The loader builds a ByteNetLM with the embedding size, model width, layer count, kernel size and dilation factor stored in each checkpoint, with final layer normalisation and no causal masking.

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: No fixed limit is stated. The paper's point is that a CNN scales linearly with sequence length and keeps performance on sequences longer than the transformer models allow.

run_guide.summary: Install the package, load a CARP checkpoint, and get per-residue representations for two short sequences.
prerequisites: PyTorch. The README says it was tested on 1.9.0, 1.11.0 and 1.12, and that pandas, scipy and wget may also be needed in a clean conda environment.
Internet access: the loader downloads the checkpoint from Zenodo on first use (2,572,014,451 bytes for carp_640M, 151,618,419 for carp_38M).
No GPU is required for the snippet; the bulk script uses one if present.

steps.title: Install
steps.explanation: The released package. The README also offers pip install git+https://github.com/microsoft/protein-sequence-models.git for the current main branch; that form cannot be pinned to a commit without changing the command.

steps.title: Load a checkpoint and encode two sequences
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from sequence_models.pretrained import load_model_and_alphabet

model, collater = load_model_and_alphabet('carp_640M')

seqs = [['MDREQ'], ['MGTRRLLP']]
x = collater(seqs)[0]  # (n, max_len)
rep = model(x)  # (n, max_len, d_model)
print(rep.shape)
PY
steps.explanation: The two README snippets joined in a shell heredoc, with a print added. The first call downloads carp_640M from Zenodo. Use carp_600k, carp_38M or carp_76M for a smaller model.

notes: The parameter values in structured are taken from the checkpoint names (carp_600k, carp_38M, carp_76M, carp_640M); no source read states an exact count, so they are the developers' rounded figures and should be treated as such. released is the date the host records for the weights (the Zenodo deposit's publication_date), the same rule used for the other models in this batch. Two Zenodo identifiers appear: the loader downloads from record 6564798, which is what was read, while the README links the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.6368483. The repository hosts MIF, MIF-ST and BiGCARP as well; only CARP is described here. Neither the Cell Systems paper nor the bioRxiv preprint (PPR496447) is open access, so only abstracts were available and no parameter counts could be sourced.
